title: SongPack v1
description: Canonical JSON Schema for the KeyQuest SongPack v1 format (plan §8.1; human spec docs/specs/songpack-v1.md). One schema, three consumers — Python pipeline (build-time validation), PHP API (publish-time validation), Kotlin tests (fixture validation) — plan §8.1.10. The root is a oneOf dispatcher over the four JSON-format-contract documents: manifest.json, notes.json, chunks.json, skills.json; consumers validate each whole file against this root. Unknown keys are ignored by clients (additive-only evolution, §8.1.9). The ONLY key explicitly forbidden anywhere is `seconds` on a note record (§8.1.1): beats are the unit of musical time and seconds appear nowhere in note data. NOTE on the forbidden-key pattern: `not: {required: ["seconds"]}` is used rather than `not: {properties: {seconds: {}}}` because the latter is vacuously valid for any object WITHOUT a seconds key — a classic draft-07 gotcha — and would reject every note. `required` checks key presence only, so it forbids `seconds` (even `seconds: null`) while leaving additionalProperties open for future keys.

note.title: note
note.description: One note (§8.1.4). Beats are the unit of musical time; seconds appear NOWHERE in note data (§8.1.1). `pitch` is the app's only pitch representation; `accidental` is display-only (pitch is absolute — a client must never derive pitch from key signature + accidental).

pitch.description: MIDI note number, A0 (21) to C8 (108). The app's only pitch representation (§8.1.4).

startBeat.description: Absolute beats from song start, pickup-adjusted (§8.1.4).

hand.description: Required; never null (§8.2.4). Used by the scorer and by LH/RH hand-isolation practice.

staff.description: Visual staff (1 = upper, 2 = lower). NOT always the hand — cross-staff passages are common and normal (§8.1.4).

finger.description: Optional; present only where the lesson teaches fingering (§8.1.4).

tieToIndex.description: Index, within this level's notes array, of the note this note ties INTO — an INDEX reference, never a beat reference (§8.1.4). Must point forward to a later note of the same pitch; the Python validator enforces this. Ties may cross chunk boundaries.

accidental.description: DISPLAY-ONLY; pitch is absolute. A client must never derive pitch from key signature + accidental (§8.1.4).

isOrnamentExpansion.description: True for notes generated from a trill/mordent (§8.1.4).

chunk.title: chunk
chunk.description: One chunk definition — the pedagogy, encoded as data (§8.1.5). teachingModes is the whole hands-separate-then-together pedagogy: ordered, the sequence the learner walks.

chunkId.description: Stable chunk identifier, unique within the pack (§8.1.5).

startBeat.description: Chunk start, absolute beats. The Python validator checks startBeat < endBeat and both within durationBeats.

endBeat.description: Chunk end, absolute beats; must be > startBeat. The Python validator checks this and that endBeat <= durationBeats.

teachingModes.description: Ordered; the sequence the learner walks (§8.1.5).

prerequisiteChunks.description: chunkIds that must be completed first (§8.1.5).

loopSafe.description: Can this chunk loop musically without a lead-in? The auto-loop suggestion skips unsafe chunks (§8.1.5).

label.description: Human-readable label shown to the user (§8.1.5).

arrangementLevel.title: arrangementLevel
arrangementLevel.description: One arrangement level (§8.1.6). Each level is a separate FULL note set in notes.json, never a diff.

level.description: 1 = Essentials, 2 = Intermediate, 3 = Pro (§8.1.6). notes.json/skills.json reference this value as its decimal string, e.g. "1".

atBeat.description: Beat at which this tempo change takes effect. The first entry MUST have atBeat 0 (the Python validator enforces it).

bpm.description: Beats per minute at this point (§8.1.3).

curve.description: step = instant change; linear = rit./accel. ramping to the next entry's bpm (§8.1.3).

atBeat.description: Beat at which this time signature takes effect. Mid-song changes are normal, not exotic (§8.1.3).

denominator.description: Beat unit as a power of two (§8.1.3).

atBeat.description: Beat at which this key signature takes effect. Mid-song changes are normal, not exotic (§8.1.3).

fifths.description: Circle of fifths: 0 = C major / A minor, +1 = G major / E minor, -1 = F major / D minor, etc.

loudnessLufs.description: Integrated loudness target, -16 LUFS across the whole catalog (§8.1.7).

micSafe.description: Mono mic-safe stem bitrate (64 kbps default, §8.1.7).

buildInfo.title: buildInfo
buildInfo.description: Build provenance (§8.1.3). REQUIRED in published packs; golden fixtures carry minimal values. Non-hashed for determinism (§8.2.10), present for support.

pipelineVersion.description: Pipeline version that built this pack.

sourceFileHash.description: Hash of the source score, e.g. "sha256:<hex>".

buildTimestamp.description: ISO-8601 UTC build time, e.g. "2026-08-24T00:00:00Z". Format is advisory in some consumers; the Python validator enforces it via FormatChecker.

gitSha.description: Git SHA of the pipeline workspace at build time.

repeatMapEntry.title: repeatMapEntry
repeatMapEntry.description: OPTIONAL manifest metadata describing a linearized repeat structure (§8.2.3). The format is linear: repeat material is already written out as notes, and loopSafe chunks mark what can loop. repeatMap is pure annotation for form visualization.

endBeat.description: Must be > startBeat; the Python validator checks this.

manifest.title: manifest.json
manifest.description: Identity, metadata, tempo map, chunk index, rights reference (§8.1.3). All fields are required unless marked optional.

format.description: Format identifier. Clients refuse anything else (§8.1.3).

songId.description: Stable identifier of the song, not the pack (§8.1.3).

packVersion.description: Increments on every publish, never reused (§8.1.3, §8.1.9).

minAppVersion.description: Clients below this refuse the pack and prompt to update (§8.1.9).

subtitle.description: Optional; most songs have no subtitle.

arranger.description: Always us, always, for public-domain works (§8.1.3).

genre.description: Library browse facet (§9.4). Vocabulary may grow additively; clients must tolerate unknown values.

era.description: Library browse facet (§9.4). Vocabulary may grow additively; clients must tolerate unknown values.

mood.description: Library browse facet (§9.4). Vocabulary may grow additively; clients must tolerate unknown values.

durationBeats.description: Total song length in beats, including pickup (§8.1.3). Beat 0 is the first pickup note. Beats are the ONLY time unit in note data (§8.1.1).

durationSecondsAtDefaultTempo.description: DISPLAY-ONLY (§8.1.1). The single allowed seconds value in the whole pack; clients must never use it for timing.

defaultTempoBpm.description: Tempo at the first tempoMap entry (§8.1.3).

minPracticeTempoPct.description: Floor for the tempo slider, as a percentage of default tempo (§8.1.3).

tempoMap.description: Chronologically ordered; the first entry MUST have atBeat 0 (the Python validator enforces it).

timeSignatures.description: Chronologically ordered; the first entry defines the opening measure.

keySignatures.description: Chronologically ordered; the first entry defines the opening key.

pickupBeats.description: Anacrusis length in beats (§8.1.3). Getting this wrong offsets the whole song by a beat — the most common single content bug, so the Python validator sanity-checks it against the opening time signature.

chunkCount.description: Number of chunks in chunks.json; the Python validator checks it equals len(chunks) (§8.1.3).

chunkIndexRef.description: Identifier of the chunk index record in chunks.json (§8.1.3).

rightsRef.description: FK into the rights record (§8.5.6). Publish is blocked without it (§8.1.3).

repeatMap.description: OPTIONAL metadata describing a linearized repeat structure (§8.2.3). Additive; clients that do not know it ignore it.

notesFile.title: notes.json
notesFile.description: The note data + layout hints, per arrangement level (§8.1.4, §8.1.6). Each level is a separate FULL note set, never a diff. Keys are the decimal string of arrangementLevels[].level. The levels MAP is deliberately strict (additionalProperties false): its keys are a closed, enumerated key space matching arrangementLevels, so an unknown key there is a content error, not a forward-compatible field; the file itself stays open for future top-level keys.

chunksFile.title: chunks.json
chunksFile.description: Chunk definitions (§8.1.5). The array is in teaching order; ord is explicit and 1-based. The array index is NOT ord.

skillLevel.title: skillLevel
skillLevel.description: Skill requirements and teachings for one arrangement level (§8.1.2 skills.json).

requiredSkills.description: Skill ids the learner must already have to play this level (§8.2.6 level-1 gate).

taughtSkills.description: Skill ids this level teaches. Chunk newSkills entries refine where.

skillsFile.title: skills.json
skillsFile.description: Skill requirements/teachings per arrangement level (§8.1.2). Keys are the decimal string of arrangementLevels[].level. As with notes.json, the levels MAP is strict while the file stays open.
